description: We’re Tech Emergers, a team from Jacobabad, Pakistan, passionate about technology, AI, space exploration, and innovation. We aim to create an interactive Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer that makes space engineering engaging and educational. We’re seeking teammates skilled in Python, AI/ML, scientific research, data analysis, game development, or UI/UX design.
summary:
Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is a free, browser-based 3D game for children aged 7–12. The player becomes the Mission Commander of an outpost on the Moon or Mars. After choosing a destination and reading a mission briefing, they manage oxygen, water, food, electricity, equipment and crew health over 3, 7 or 30 days.

Each day the player chooses an operation, such as making oxygen, recycling water, growing food or repairing equipment. They must also respond to events like dust storms, radiation warnings and communication delays. Every choice has a cost, a benefit and a science explanation.

The Moon and Mars play differently. Lunar oxygen is locked in rock and needs a lot of power. Mars oxygen can be made from carbon dioxide, inspired by NASA’s MOXIE experiment.

The game teaches the real trade-offs of space exploration through play. 3D child astronauts, a read-aloud button, bigger text and a phone-friendly design make it easy for more children to use. Resource numbers are simplified game units, not real mission data.
details:
Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an educational, space-themed 3D game designed to introduce children to the challenges of managing a human settlement on the Moon and Mars.

The project places the player in the role of a Mission Commander, responsible for managing an astronaut outpost and making decisions that affect the survival and success of the mission. Players explore a simulated space environment, interact with different mission systems, and learn about essential resources such as oxygen, water, electricity, and food.

How It Works

Players begin by selecting a mission: Lunar or Martian. After receiving their mission briefing, they enter a simulated 3D outpost where they must understand the environment, manage available resources, and respond to mission challenges.

The game introduces resource management, decision-making, exploration, and problem-solving. Players learn that every resource is limited and that their decisions can have consequences for the crew and the mission. The experience aims to encourage experimentation, strategic thinking, and scientific curiosity.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The project aims to:

  • Make space science more engaging and accessible to children.
  • Introduce the challenges of human exploration beyond Earth.
  • Develop critical thinking, decision-making, and problem-solving skills.
  • Teach the importance of conserving and managing limited resources.
  • Encourage interest in astronomy, engineering, technology, and STEM education.

Our long-term vision is to make complex space exploration concepts understandable through interactive learning rather than relying only on textbooks and memorization.

Tools and Technologies

The project was developed using web technologies and 3D development tools, including:

  • HTML5 for the application structure.
  • CSS3 for interface design and responsive layouts.
  • JavaScript for game logic and interactivity.
  • Three.js for 3D graphics and environmental visualization.
  • Netlify for hosting and public access.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of this project is its attempt to turn the responsibilities of an astronaut into an interactive learning experience. Instead of simply presenting facts about the Moon and Mars, the game encourages children to take responsibility for a simulated outpost and understand the trade-offs involved in sustaining human life in space.

The two mission environments introduce different planetary conditions and scientific challenges, helping learners understand that exploring the Moon and Mars requires different approaches.

Factors Considered

During development, our team considered:

  • Scientific accuracy and the differences between lunar and Martian environments.
  • The limited availability of essential resources during space missions.
  • Age-appropriate explanations and gameplay for young learners.
  • Mobile accessibility and ease of navigation.
  • The importance of interactive learning and meaningful consequences.
  • Performance and accessibility through a web browser.

Our mission: To inspire the next generation of explorers by allowing children to experience the responsibility, challenges, and excitement of managing a mission beyond Earth.
